function: Joint learning of BS beamforming vector, RSMA user transmit powers, and BS/CS computational rates for sensing-constrained computational rate maximization (p. 5).
system: Uplink ISAC-MEC: BS with N=8 antennas, K=3 single-antenna users (K varies 2-6), one cloud server, RSMA, no RIS; 30 MHz, wavelength 0.08 m (pp. 2, 7).
method: Soft actor-critic deep reinforcement learning (SAC-BCP): fully connected actor and two critics, trained from interaction with replay buffer; reward is change in sum computational rate (p. 6).
data_channel: Custom simulator: i.i.d. Rayleigh flat fading (zero mean, unit variance) for user-BS and BS-CS links, path loss 30+30log10(d); no dataset or measurements; online simulated interaction (pp. 3, 7).
test_conditions: Training convergence shown per K (2 to 6); results swept over K, minimum sensing SINR, BS power 21-43 dBm, bandwidth 10-50 MHz; no unseen scenario tested (pp. 7-9).
baselines: NOMA-BCP, RSMA-FP (RSMA, fixed power), NOMA-FP (NOMA, fixed power, after [13]); all variants of the same joint design; no other learned or classical algorithm compared (p. 7).
metrics: Computational data rate (Mbps) versus users, minimum sensing SINR, BS power, bandwidth; percent gain over baselines; convergence episodes (pp. 7-9).
complexity: Big-O training complexity per step (Eq. 40) and over T iterations (Eq. 41), from products of adjacent layer sizes of actor and critics (pp. 6-7); no runtime reported.
q1_support: p. 3: "experience Rayleigh flat fading" - custom i.i.d. Rayleigh model with path loss L = 30 + 30 log10(d) on p. 7; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 7: "More importantly, as K increases from 2 to 6, the required" convergence episodes are reported per K (Fig. 2); results sweep K, minimum sensing SINR, BS power and bandwidth, and the paper never tests a trained model in a condition unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 7: "RSMA-FP: Use RSMA for the considered system with" fixed power; the baselines NOMA-BCP, RSMA-FP and NOMA-FP only change the multiple access or fix the power of the same joint design, so they are variants of the proposed method; the paper names no earlier learned method (such as DDPG or PPO) and states no non-learned algorithm as baseline.
q4_support: p. 6: "The computational complexity for each training step is" O(3 sum K^pi_{j-1} K^pi_j + 6 sum K^Q_{j-1} K^Q_j), Eq. (40), and the total over T training iterations is Eq. (41) on p. 7.
q5_support: p. 7: "we provide numerical results to evaluate the" proposed scheme; channels are simulated with the parameters of Table I; no code or data link, no public dataset, and no measured data is given.
notes: Borderline above_phy, included under the rule that a work learning a physical-layer decision jointly with one above it passes: the SAC action holds BS/CS computational rates (above PHY) plus the BS beamformer and user powers (PHY), p. 5. Area 5 because the beamformer p serves sensing and CS offloading under a sensing SINR constraint (pp. 3-5). Table I values (N=8, K=3, B=30 MHz, lambda=0.08 m) read from the image of p. 7; the carrier frequency is not stated as such. NOMA-FP cites [13] but the paper does not say how any baseline is solved.
